newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha bounces up,inter-month spreads widen.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha bounces up,inter-month spreads widen.

text.p: Naphtha prices rebounded in afternoon Tokyo trade on Wednesday, tracking overnight crudes, which gained ground in a rally led by heating oil.
Bids for first-half February open-spec naphtha were assessed at $223.00, with offers at $224.50, up sharply from late Tuesday's $218.00/221.00.
Second-half January was assessed at $225.50/227.00. It was traded at $221.00 in Tuesday evening trading.
Inter-month naphtha spreads broadened, with first-half January/first-hlaf February indicated at plus $5.00/6.00, compared with Tuesday's plus $4.00/5.00.
In the low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) market, Indonesia's initial allocation for December lifting is expected to total around 3.5 million tonnes, fuel oil traders said.
State-owned Pertamina will announce its December allocation by the end of the week, they said.
Pertamina alloted 3.6 million tonnes in its initial allocation for November lifting.

Japan's December demand for Pertamina cargoes is estimated at 800,000 to one million barrels, traders said. Extra requirments will emerge if temperatures drop sharply, boosting LSWR demand from thermal power plants.--Tokyo Energy Desk
